answer: An echo returns only what another sent, so credit must trace to a source. Identity needs two holders outside its own karst to countersign the original call, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses instead of one crew. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A lantern audit replays a random call each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim voids the whole karst and forfeits its bonds, which cannot be pooled or resold.
